explain.why: Read the scale that starts at 0 on the other side.
Was one 10° interval out.
Was one 10° interval out.

solution: Start at the 0° mark that QP lies on and read along that scale.

questions.stem: In the figure, AOB is a straight line. ∠AOC = 57°. Find ∠COB.

explain.why: Gave the angle that was already known.
Made a slip of 10 in the final subtraction.

questions.stem: In the figure, AOB is a straight line. ∠AOC = 98°. Find ∠COB.

explain.why: Made a slip of 10 in the final subtraction.
Gave the angle that was already known.

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus. ∠PQR = 88°. Find ∠QPR.

explain.why: Gave ∠QPS instead of halving it for ∠QPR.
Subtracted the angle from 90° instead of finding the base angle.
Halved the given angle instead of using the isosceles triangle.

solution: All sides of a rhombus are equal, so triangle PQR is isosceles with QP = QR.
The two base angles are equal: ∠QPR = (180° − 88°) ÷ 2 = 46°

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus. ∠PQR = 66°. Find ∠QPR.

explain.why: Gave ∠QPS instead of halving it for ∠QPR.
Halved the given angle instead of using the isosceles triangle.
Subtracted the angle from 90° instead of finding the base angle.

solution: All sides of a rhombus are equal, so triangle PQR is isosceles with QP = QR.
The two base angles are equal: ∠QPR = (180° − 66°) ÷ 2 = 57°

questions.stem: Hui Min wants to draw ∠PQR = 95°, with QP along the baseline of the protractor pointing to the right. Hui Min marks R at 95 on the inner scale (the scale that starts at 0 on the left). What is the actual size of ∠PQR in the drawing?

explain.why: Was one 10° interval out.
Took the inner scale reading as the angle even though QP is not on its 0°.
Made a small arithmetic slip.

solution: QP is on the right, so the 0° mark for this angle is on the right.
The mark R is at 95 on the inner scale, so on the other scale it reads 180° - 95° = 85°.

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus. ∠PQR = 68°. Find ∠QPR.

explain.why: Gave ∠QPS instead of halving it for ∠QPR.
Halved the given angle instead of using the isosceles triangle.
Subtracted the angle from 90° instead of finding the base angle.

solution: All sides of a rhombus are equal, so triangle PQR is isosceles with QP = QR.
The two base angles are equal: ∠QPR = (180° − 68°) ÷ 2 = 56°

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus. ∠PQR = 74°. Find ∠QPR.

explain.why: Gave ∠QPS instead of halving it for ∠QPR.
Halved the given angle instead of using the isosceles triangle.
Subtracted the angle from 90° instead of finding the base angle.

solution: All sides of a rhombus are equal, so triangle PQR is isosceles with QP = QR.
The two base angles are equal: ∠QPR = (180° − 74°) ÷ 2 = 53°

explain.why: Was one 10° interval out.
Was one 10° interval out.

solution: QP is on the right, so the 0° mark for this angle is on the right.
The mark R is at 50 on the inner scale, so on the other scale it reads 180° - 50° = 130°.

explain.why: Subtracted from 180° instead of 360°.
Subtracted an extra 90°.

explain.why: Found ∠COB instead of ∠BOD.
Added the constant to the wrong angle.

explain.why: Counted the nets that do not fold into a cube.
Accepted a net where two faces overlap.
Rejected a valid net.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

explain.why: Rejected a valid net.
Accepted a net where two faces overlap.
Miscounted.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

explain.why: Accepted a net where two faces overlap.
Rejected a valid net.
Miscounted.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

explain.why: Used 2 × base sides.
Added one.
Stopped at the number of sides of the base.

solution: Base has n sides: a pyramid has edges 2n, vertices n + 1, faces n + 1.

solution: Base has n sides: a prism has edges 3n, vertices 2n, faces n + 2.

explain.why: Rejected a valid net.
Miscounted.
Accepted a net where two faces overlap.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

explain.why: Miscounted.
Rejected a valid net.
Accepted a net where two faces overlap.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

explain.why: Miscounted.
Accepted a net where two faces overlap.
Rejected a valid net.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

explain.why: Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.
Subtracted the apex angle from 180° and stopped.
Found the base angle ∠PRQ but not the angle outside the triangle.

QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 44° = 136°

explain.why: Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.
Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.

solution: Sides of a rhombus and of an equilateral triangle are all equal, so SP = SR = ST.
∠PST = 100° + 60° = 160°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

questions.stem: PQRS is a rectangular piece of paper. It is folded along UV so that P falls on P′ and Q falls on Q′, as shown. ∠PUV = 132°. Find ∠RVQ′.

explain.why: Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.
Found ∠UVQ and stopped.
Gave the given angle.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 132° = 48° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 48°.
∠UVR = 132° (angles on a straight line with ∠UVQ), so ∠RVQ′ = 132° − 48° = 84°

questions.stem: PQR is an isosceles triangle with PQ = PR and ∠QPR = 50°. The side QR is extended to S. Find ∠PRS.

explain.why: Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.
Subtracted the apex angle from 180° and stopped.
Found the base angle ∠PRQ but not the angle outside the triangle.

solution: PQ = PR, so the base angles are equal.
QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 65° = 115°

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus and RST is an equilateral triangle. ∠PSR = 76°. Find ∠SPT.

explain.why: Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.
Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.

solution: Sides of a rhombus and of an equilateral triangle are all equal, so SP = SR = ST.
∠PST = 76° + 60° = 136°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

explain.why: Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.
Gave the given angle.
Found ∠UVQ and stopped.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 136° = 44° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 44°.
∠UVR = 136° (angles on a straight line with ∠UVQ), so ∠RVQ′ = 136° − 44° = 92°

questions.stem: The corner A of a rectangular sheet is folded along AE so that AB falls on AB′, as shown by the dotted line. ∠B′AD = 54°. Find ∠BAE.

explain.why: Gave the complement of the answer.

Gave the given angle.

questions.stem: PQR is an isosceles triangle with PQ = PR and ∠QPR = 60°. The side QR is extended to S. Find ∠PRS.

explain.why: Made a slip of 10 in the final subtraction.
Found the base angle ∠PRQ but not the angle outside the triangle.
Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.

solution: PQ = PR, so the base angles are equal.
QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 60° = 120°

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus and RST is an equilateral triangle. ∠PSR = 66°. Find ∠SPT.

explain.why: Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.
Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.

solution: Sides of a rhombus and of an equilateral triangle are all equal, so SP = SR = ST.
∠PST = 66° + 60° = 126°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

questions.stem: PQRS is a rectangular piece of paper. It is folded along UV so that P falls on P′ and Q falls on Q′, as shown. ∠PUV = 138°. Find ∠RVQ′.

explain.why: Gave the given angle.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.
Found ∠UVQ and stopped.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 138° = 42° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 42°.
∠UVR = 138° (angles on a straight line with ∠UVQ), so ∠RVQ′ = 138° − 42° = 96°

explain.why: Subtracted the apex angle from 180° and stopped.
Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.

QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 61° = 119°

explain.why: Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.
Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.

∠PST = 96° + 60° = 156°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

questions.stem: PQRS is a rectangular piece of paper. It is folded along UV so that P falls on P′ and Q falls on Q′, as shown. ∠PUV = 124°. Find ∠RVQ′.

explain.why: Found ∠UVQ and stopped.
Gave the given angle.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 124° = 56° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 56°.
∠UVR = 124° (angles on a straight line with ∠UVQ), so ∠RVQ′ = 124° − 56° = 68°

Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.

explain.why: Found ∠UVQ and stopped.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.
Gave the given angle.

questions.stem: PQR is an isosceles triangle with PQ = PR and ∠QPR = 56°. The side QR is extended to S. Find ∠PRS.

explain.why: Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.
Found the base angle ∠PRQ but not the angle outside the triangle.
Subtracted the apex angle from 180° and stopped.

solution: PQ = PR, so the base angles are equal.
QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 62° = 118°

explain.why: Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.
Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.

explain.why: Gave the given angle.
Found ∠UVQ and stopped.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 134° = 46° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 46°.

explain.why: Found the base angle ∠PRQ but not the angle outside the triangle.
Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.

QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 67° = 113°

explain.why: Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.
Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.

∠PST = 88° + 60° = 148°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

questions.stem: PQRS is a rectangular piece of paper. It is folded along UV so that P falls on P′ and Q falls on Q′, as shown. ∠PUV = 120°. Find ∠RVQ′.

explain.why: Made a slip of 10 in the final subtraction.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.
Subtracted 90° from the given angle.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 120° = 60° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 60°.
∠UVR = 120° (angles on a straight line with ∠UVQ), so ∠RVQ′ = 120° − 60° = 60°

explain.why: Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.
Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.

solution: Sides of a rhombus and of an equilateral triangle are all equal, so SP = SR = ST.
∠PST = 54° + 60° = 114°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

explain.why: Found ∠UVQ and stopped.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.
Gave the given angle.

questions.stem: PQR is an isosceles triangle with PQ = PR and ∠QPR = 36°. The side QR is extended to S. Find ∠PRS.

explain.why: Subtracted the apex angle from 180° and stopped.
Halved the apex angle before subtracting from 180°.
Found the base angle ∠PRQ but not the angle outside the triangle.

solution: PQ = PR, so the base angles are equal.
QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 72° = 108°

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus and RST is an equilateral triangle. ∠PSR = 52°. Find ∠SPT.

explain.why: Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.
Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.
Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.

∠PST = 52° + 60° = 112°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

explain.why: Gave the given angle.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.
Found ∠UVQ and stopped.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 114° = 66° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 66°.
∠UVR = 114° (angles on a straight line with ∠UVQ), so ∠RVQ′ = 114° − 66° = 48°

Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

questions.stem: PQR is an isosceles triangle with PQ = PR and ∠QPR = 90°. The side QR is extended to S. Find ∠PRS.

explain.why: Subtracted the apex angle from 180° and stopped.
Made a slip of 10 in the final subtraction.
Found the base angle ∠PRQ but not the angle outside the triangle.

solution: PQ = PR, so the base angles are equal.
QRS is a straight line, so ∠PRS = 180° − 45° = 135°

questions.stem: PQRS is a rhombus and RST is an equilateral triangle. ∠PSR = 56°. Find ∠SPT.

explain.why: Left out the 60° angle of the equilateral triangle.
Found ∠SPT + ∠STP but did not halve it.
Gave ∠PST, the angle at S.

solution: Sides of a rhombus and of an equilateral triangle are all equal, so SP = SR = ST.
∠PST = 56° + 60° = 116°; triangle SPT is isosceles with SP = ST

questions.stem: PQRS is a rectangular piece of paper. It is folded along UV so that P falls on P′ and Q falls on Q′, as shown. ∠PUV = 122°. Find ∠RVQ′.

explain.why: Found ∠UVQ and stopped.
Gave the given angle.
Found ∠QVQ′ instead of ∠RVQ′.

solution: PS is parallel to QR, so ∠UVQ = 180° − 122° = 58° (co-interior angles).
A fold does not change angles, so ∠UVQ′ = ∠UVQ = 58°.
∠UVR = 122° (angles on a straight line with ∠UVQ), so ∠RVQ′ = 122° − 58° = 64°

questions.stem: Ali joins a square of side 13 cm to a rectangle of length 4 cm and breadth 10 cm, as shown. The bottoms of the two shapes are level. Find the perimeter of the whole figure in cm.

explain.why: Left out one side.
Added the perimeters of the two shapes, counting the joined side twice.
Made a slip of 10 in the final subtraction.

solution: Total length across the bottom = 4 + 13 = 17 cm

questions.stem: Farid marks the points G, H, W, X, Y and Z on a square grid. Which point, when joined to G and H, forms a right-angled triangle?

explain.why: Triangle GHZ has no right angle (its largest angle is about 121°).
Triangle GHY has no right angle (its largest angle is about 70°).
Triangle GHX has no right angle (its largest angle is about 166°).

solution: A right-angled triangle has one corner that is a right angle.

That shape has two pairs of parallel sides; a trapezium has exactly one pair.

questions.stem: Xin Yi draws Triangle R on a square grid. What type of triangle is Triangle R?

explain.why: No two of its sides are the same length.
Its three sides are not all the same length.
It has a right angle, but the two sides that make the right angle are not equal.

solution: At one corner, one side goes 3 across and 3 up and the other goes 1 across and 1 up: one is the other turned through a right angle, so that corner is a right angle.
The three sides all have different lengths.
Triangle R is a right-angled triangle.

questions.stem: Jun Wei marks the points J, K, W, X, Y and Z on a square grid. Which point, when joined to J and K, forms an isosceles triangle?

explain.why: No two sides of triangle JKZ are the same length.
No two sides of triangle JKY are the same length.
No two sides of triangle JKW are the same length.

solution: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides.
JK and JX each go 4 squares one way and 2 the other way, so they are the same length.
So X forms an isosceles triangle with J and K.

questions.stem: Wei Jie marks the points E, F, W, X, Y and Z on a square grid. Which point, when joined to E and F, forms a right-angled triangle?

explain.why: Triangle EFX has no right angle (its largest angle is about 108°).
Triangle EFY has no right angle (its largest angle is about 135°).
Triangle EFW has no right angle (its largest angle is about 162°).

solution: A right-angled triangle has one corner that is a right angle.
At F, one side goes 5 down and the other goes 2 across: they meet at a right angle.
So Z forms a right-angled triangle with E and F.

questions.stem: Kumar draws five lines, P, Q, R, S and T, on a square grid. Which two lines are parallel to each other?

explain.why: Lines P and Q would meet at about 18° if they were drawn longer, so they are not parallel.
Lines P and S would meet at about 18° if they were drawn longer, so they are not parallel.
Lines R and T would meet at about 27° if they were drawn longer, so they are not parallel.

solution: Parallel lines slope the same way, so they never meet however long they are drawn.
Line Q goes 1 across for every 2 down. Line S goes 1 across for every 2 down.

questions.stem: Farid draws five lines, P, Q, R, S and T, on a square grid. Which two lines are perpendicular to each other?

explain.why: Lines P and S would meet at about 72°, not at a right angle.
Lines P and T would meet at about 63°, not at a right angle.
Lines P and R would meet at about 63°, not at a right angle.

solution: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle (or would, if they were drawn longer).
Line Q goes 3 across for every 1 down. Line T goes 1 across for every 3 up.
Turning line Q through a right angle gives the direction of line T, so lines Q and T are perpendicular.

Lines P and Q would meet at about 72°, not at a right angle.

questions.stem: Ali draws five lines, P, Q, R, S and T, on a square grid. Which two lines are parallel to each other?

explain.why: Lines Q and T would meet at about 18° if they were drawn longer, so they are not parallel.
Lines P and Q would meet at about 18° if they were drawn longer, so they are not parallel.
Lines Q and R would meet at about 18° if they were drawn longer, so they are not parallel.

solution: Parallel lines slope the same way, so they never meet however long they are drawn.
Line P goes 1 across for every 2 up. Line T goes 1 across for every 2 up.
So lines P and T are parallel.

questions.stem: Arjun draws five lines, P, Q, R, S and T, on a square grid. Which two lines are perpendicular to each other?

explain.why: Lines Q and S are parallel: they slope the same way and never meet.
Lines S and T would meet at about 72°, not at a right angle.
Lines Q and T would meet at about 72°, not at a right angle.

solution: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle (or would, if they were drawn longer).
Line P goes 1 across for every 1 up. Line T goes 1 across for every 1 down.
Turning line P through a right angle gives the direction of line T, so lines P and T are perpendicular.
